title: Pneumatic Conveying System

introduction.definition: A pneumatic conveying system transports powders and granules through a closed pipeline using air (or nitrogen). In a dilute-phase pressure system, a blower supplies air, a rotary airlock feeds the solids into the line, and the particles are carried in suspension at high air velocity. At the destination, a receiver with a bag filter separates the solids from the air and drops them into the silo.
applications: Cement, fly ash and flour transfer
key_points: Dilute phase: high velocity (≈ 15–30 m/s), particles suspended
Dense phase: low velocity, plugs/dunes — gentler, less wear
Bends are the main wear and degradation points

foundation: Support the conveyor stringers and drive frames on steelwork or plinths designed for belt tension, material load and drive torque.
alignment: Survey the structure so all pulleys and idlers are square to the centre line; train the belt empty, then loaded.
piping: Use long-radius or special wear-resistant bends; align flanges perfectly (steps cause wear and blockages).
Fit pressure transmitters along the line and a pressure relief on the blower; earth the pipeline (static).
commissioning: Check pull-wire emergency stops, belt-drift and speed switches; run empty and loaded; record take-up position and motor current.

routine.task: Monitor line pressure and blower current.

periodic.task: Check bends for wear (thickness gauging); check filter ΔP.

overhaul.task: Replace filter bags, bends and airlock rotor.

lubrication: Blower: oil level and change interval; airlock bearings greased.

causes: Air velocity too low, overfeeding, moisture
remedies: Clear; increase air or reduce feed; dry air

safety: Dust explosion risk with combustible dusts — earthing, explosion venting/suppression per ATEX/NFPA; relief valves on pressure sources.

script.narration: This module introduces the Pneumatic Conveying System.
A pneumatic conveying system transports powders and granules through a closed pipeline using air (or nitrogen).
In a dilute-phase pressure system, a blower supplies air, a rotary airlock feeds the solids into the line, and the particles are carried in suspension at high air velocity.
At the destination, a receiver with a bag filter separates the solids from the air and drops them into the silo.
Typical applications include cement, fly ash and flour transfer; plastic pellets and powders; food and pharmaceutical powders; bulk tanker unloading.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

script.narration: How the Pneumatic Conveying System works.
The blower supplies conveying air.
The rotary airlock feeds solids from the hopper into the air stream.
Particles are carried along the pipeline and around long-radius bends.
The receiver and bag filter separate solids from the air; solids drop into the silo.
The silo stores the delivered material.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Pneumatic Conveying System.
Monitor line pressure and blower current.
Check bends for wear (thickness gauging); check filter ΔP.
Replace filter bags, bends and airlock rotor.
Watch for line blockage: rising pressure, no delivery. Common cause: air velocity too low, overfeeding, moisture.
Watch for bend wear-through: leaks, dust. Common cause: abrasive material at high velocity.
Watch for filter blinding: high ΔP, back-pressure. Common cause: moist air, cleaning failure.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
